entities.summary: Valentinus was a prominent early Christian Gnostic theologian who founded his school in Rome and gained a significant following, but his theology was eventually deemed heretical and he started his own group when another was chosen for the bishopric of Rome. According to Tertullian, Valentinus was a key figure in the development of Gnosticism, which emphasized the importance of spiritual knowledge and the struggle between the material and spiritual worlds. His teachings had a profound impact on the early Christian church, influencing the development of various Gnostic sects and sparking debates about the nature of God and the role of the divine in human life. Valentinus' legacy can still be seen in the many Gnostic texts that have survived to this day, including the Gospel of Thomas and the Apocryphon of John. Despite his significant influence, Valentinus' own theological views were ultimately deemed to be too radical for the mainstream Christian church, leading to his exclusion from the church's official dogma.
